headline: High-risk workflow automation pair: n8n’s server-side execution and broad egress create dangerous default paths for leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors; marker adds no blocking controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker has no shared channel or tool surface, so it cannot directly inject n8n by default. The only plausible bridge is manual handoff of document content into n8n workflows, which is an unusual configuration and limited by the document-processing role of marker and n8n’s workflow inputs.
conditions: IF marker output is manually pasted into an n8n workflow input, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF n8n workflows parse untrusted document text as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep marker outputs as data, not instructions.
Add a fixed delimiter/schema before n8n ingests text.
Require human review before any AI Agent node runs.
Use a separate staging workflow for untrusted documents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n can read and write the server filesystem and send data through broad integration nodes, while marker is a document-processing tool with no network egress or filesystem access. In default n8n workflows, document contents can flow into third-party services, so sensitive data touched by the workflow may leak even though marker itself is local-only.
conditions: IF an n8n workflow processes sensitive documents and uses an external integration node, leakage is plausible.
IF marker outputs are stored on the n8n server filesystem, they can be re-read by workflows.
mitigations: Restrict n8n credentials to least privilege.
Disable or gate external integration nodes for sensitive workflows.
Store sensitive outputs outside the shared server filesystem.
Add a manual approval step before any outbound node.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker has no write or network capabilities, but n8n has server filesystem write, shell execution, and subprocess spawning. That creates overlapping authority over shared mutable resources in n8n’s execution environment, so concurrent workflows can conflict even though marker itself cannot write. Uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this above low.
conditions: IF two n8n executions target the same files or connected systems, write conflicts can occur.
IF marker outputs are fed into n8n jobs that mutate shared state, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Serialize workflows that touch the same files.
Use per-run unique output paths.
Add locking around shared datastore writes.
Avoid Execute Command for shared resources unless necessary.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker produces document-processing outputs that n8n can treat as workflow inputs, and n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate downstream actions. Without an explicit verification step, n8n may act on marker output as authoritative, so a parsing or extraction error can cascade into incorrect emails, API calls, or file writes.
conditions: IF n8n uses marker output as a trigger or decision input without validation, cascading error is possible.
IF downstream nodes send emails, update records, or call APIs, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a validation node between marker and action nodes.
Require schema checks on marker output.
Add human approval before irreversible actions.
Log and diff extracted fields against source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n’s docs indicate server-side processing with per-credential secrets and connected systems, while marker is a document-processing component with no stated residency or retention controls. If regulated data enters n8n workflows, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches; marker is not the compliance driver, so it is cited only as the upstream document source.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated data and n8n stores it on the server, retention mismatch is possible.
IF EU personal data is routed through non-EU integrations, residency risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before it enters n8n.
Set short retention on workflow logs and executions.
Avoid storing regulated payloads in credentials or execution history.
Use region-appropriate integrations only.
